## Introduction

my skills at Data Summarization/Exploratory Analysis/Table Formatting in an analysis of Media/Internet data.

## Data Acquisition and Preparation

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#' Acquire Netflix What We Watched Reports
#'
#' This function will acquire and standardize all data for MP#01
#' from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#' are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#' relevant files (with CDN hash).
#'
#' After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#' performed.
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
  
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
  
    return(local)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS |>
    map(read_html) |>
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |>
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |>
    enframe("period", "url") |>
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")),
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed),
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"),
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |>
    select(-url, -path) |>
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4),
           half=str_sub(period, start=6),
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1),
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |>
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |>
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"),
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)),
           .by=Title,
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"),
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year,
           period,
           period_start,
           period_end,
           Title,
           -half,
           Runtime,
           Views,
           `Hours Viewed`,
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`,
           live_event)
}

NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()
```

```{r}
# Task 2: rename columns to tidy snake_case names
# Task 3: convert year to integer and global availability to TRUE/FALSE
NETFLIX_DATA <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  rename(
    title              = Title,
    runtime            = Runtime,
    views              = Views,
    hours_viewed       = `Hours Viewed`,
    release_date       = `Release Date`,
    available_globally = `Available Globally?`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year               = as.integer(year),
    available_globally = available_globally == "Yes"
  )
```

### Exploratory Questions

```{r}
library(scales)

# Q1: date range covered
date_start <- min(NETFLIX_DATA$period_start)
date_end   <- max(NETFLIX_DATA$period_end)

# Q2: number of distinct titles
n_titles <- n_distinct(NETFLIX_DATA$title)

# Q3: Bridgerton universe hours
bridgerton_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Bridgerton")) |>
  summarize(total = sum(hours_viewed)) |>
  pull(total)

# Q4: the five main Stranger Things seasons only
stranger_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Stranger Things")) |>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Beyond")) |>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Tales")) |>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Fireplace")) |>
  summarize(total = sum(hours_viewed)) |>
  pull(total)

# Q5: share of 2026H1 watch time captured by its top 10 titles
h1_2026     <- NETFLIX_DATA |> filter(period == "2026H1")
top10_share <- h1_2026 |>
  slice_max(hours_viewed, n = 10) |>
  summarize(share = sum(hours_viewed)) |>
  pull(share) / sum(h1_2026$hours_viewed)

# Q6: share of catalog available globally, by title and by hours
global_by_title <- mean(NETFLIX_DATA$available_globally, na.rm = TRUE)
global_by_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(!is.na(available_globally)) |>
  summarize(share = sum(hours_viewed[available_globally]) / sum(hours_viewed)) |>
  pull(share)
```

1. The range covered in this data is `r format(date_start, "%B %d, %Y")` to `r format(date_end, "%B %d, %Y")`.
2. There are `r comma(n_titles)` different shows and movies in this data set.
3. There have been `r comma(bridgerton_hours)` total hours watched in the Bridgerton universe.
4. There have been `r comma(stranger_hours)` total hours spent watching the five seasons of Stranger Things.
5. In the first half of 2026, the top 10 titles accounted for `r percent(top10_share, 0.1)` of all viewing.
6. Of all titles in Netflix's catalog, `r percent(global_by_title, 0.1)` are globally available. These titles account for `r percent(global_by_hours, 0.1)` of total hours viewed.

### Exploratory Tables

```{r}
#| message: false
library(gt)
SOURCE_NOTE <- "Source: Netflix 'What We Watched' engagement reports, 2023H1–2026H1."
```

#### Top Title in Each Period

```{r}
# Task 6.1: top title per period and its share of that period's total hours
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(period_total = sum(hours_viewed), .by = period) |>
  slice_max(hours_viewed, n = 1, by = period, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  transmute(period, title, hours_viewed,
            share = hours_viewed / period_total) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Top Netflix Title in Each Six-Month Period",
             subtitle = "Ranked by total hours viewed") |>
  cols_label(period = "Period", title = "Title",
             hours_viewed = "Hours Viewed",
             share = "Share of Period Viewing") |>
  fmt_number(hours_viewed, suffixing = TRUE, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_percent(share, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_source_note(SOURCE_NOTE)
```

#### Catalog Size Over Time

```{r}
# Task 6.2: number of titles and total runtime per period
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(n_titles      = n_distinct(title),
            runtime_hours = sum(runtime, na.rm = TRUE) / 60,
            .by = period) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Size of Netflix's Reported Catalog by Period",
             subtitle = "Number of titles and total runtime of content") |>
  cols_label(period = "Period", n_titles = "Number of Titles",
             runtime_hours = "Total Runtime (Hours)") |>
  fmt_number(n_titles, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(runtime_hours, suffixing = TRUE, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_source_note(SOURCE_NOTE) |>
  tab_source_note("Runtime excludes titles with no published runtime (about 21% of rows).")
```

#### Most Consistent "Comfort Food" Titles

```{r}
# Task 6.3: titles present in every period, ranked by their worst period.
# A high minimum means the title never had a weak period; a low
# coefficient of variation (sd / mean) means viewing was steady.
n_periods_total <- n_distinct(NETFLIX_DATA$period)

NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(n_periods = n_distinct(period),
            avg_hours = mean(hours_viewed),
            min_hours = min(hours_viewed),
            sd_hours  = sd(hours_viewed),
            .by = title) |>
  filter(n_periods == n_periods_total) |>
  mutate(cv = sd_hours / avg_hours) |>
  slice_max(min_hours, n = 10) |>
  select(title, avg_hours, min_hours, cv) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Netflix's Most Consistent Titles",
             subtitle = "Titles in all seven periods, ranked by their lowest period") |>
  cols_label(title = "Title", avg_hours = "Avg. Hours per Period",
             min_hours = "Lowest Period (Hours)",
             cv = "Variability (CV)") |>
  fmt_number(c(avg_hours, min_hours), suffixing = TRUE, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(cv, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_source_note(SOURCE_NOTE) |>
  tab_source_note("CV = standard deviation / mean; lower values mean steadier viewership.")
```

YOUR EXPLANATION OF TABLE 3 GOES HERE

#### Shows vs. Movies

```{r}
# Task 6.4: classify titles. Live events are their own category; otherwise
# a title is a show if it has "Season", "Series", or "Limited" in the name
# or runs longer than 4 hours (240 minutes); everything else is a movie.
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    live_event ~ "Live Event",
    str_detect(title, "Season|Series|Limited") ~ "Show",
    coalesce(runtime > 240, FALSE) ~ "Show",
    TRUE ~ "Movie")) |>
  summarize(hours = sum(hours_viewed), .by = c(period, type)) |>
  mutate(share = hours / sum(hours), .by = period) |>
  select(period, type, share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Share of Viewing Time: Shows vs. Movies",
             subtitle = "Percent of each period's total hours viewed") |>
  cols_label(period = "Period") |>
  fmt_percent(-period, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_source_note(SOURCE_NOTE) |>
  tab_source_note("Shows: titles containing 'Season', 'Series', or 'Limited', or longer than 4 hours.")
```

YOUR EXPLANATION OF TABLE 4 GOES HERE

#### Live Events vs. Pre-Taped Content

```{r}
# Task 6.5: average and top-tier performance of live vs pre-taped content.
# Views (hours / runtime) adjusts for length, since live events are short.
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(type = if_else(live_event, "Live Event", "Pre-Taped")) |>
  summarize(n_entries  = n(),
            avg_hours  = mean(hours_viewed),
            avg_views  = mean(views, na.rm = TRUE),
            top10_hours = mean(head(sort(hours_viewed, decreasing = TRUE), 10)),
            top10_views = mean(head(sort(views, decreasing = TRUE), 10)),
            .by = type) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Live Events vs. Pre-Taped Content",
             subtitle = "Average title vs. top-10 titles in each group") |>
  cols_label(type = "Content Type", n_entries = "Entries",
             avg_hours = "Avg. Hours", avg_views = "Avg. Views",
             top10_hours = "Top-10 Avg. Hours",
             top10_views = "Top-10 Avg. Views") |>
  fmt_number(n_entries, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(-c(type, n_entries), suffixing = TRUE, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_source_note(SOURCE_NOTE) |>
  tab_source_note("Views are Netflix's estimate (hours viewed / runtime); unavailable for 2023H1.")
```
